jd_full:
About Pell Frischmann
A specialist advisory and technical consultancy across the built and natural environment, serving public and private-sector clients in buildings, infrastructure and regeneration. Formed in 1926; part of RSBG SE.
Appointment Type: Permanent
Full-time, 37.5 hours
Specialism: Business Administration
Location: Wakefield, Birmingham, London, Manchester
Working Practice: Hybrid
Job Reference: 10925
Main Purpose of the Job
The Business Analyst will support the maintenance and continuous improvement of AI tools, AI agents and organisational knowledge assets, while helping project teams prepare for audits. The role will also support business-wide reporting for all functions, turning data from multiple sources into accurate, timely reports, dashboards and insights.
This role is suited to a recent graduate, or someone with up to two years' experience who is interested in artificial intelligence, information management, data quality, project assurance and digital transformation. The successful candidate will work with business teams, project managers, subject-matter experts and developers to keep information accurate, controlled, accessible and audit-ready.
Main Duties and Responsibilities
• Maintain AI knowledge sources, prompts, instructions and repositories, reviewing information for accuracy, completeness and ownership.
• Support AI agent testing, monitoring, issue logging and controlled updates, managing version control, metadata, taxonomy and governance registers.
• Maintain audit trails, approval records and change logs in line with internal AI policies and data governance requirements.
• Help project teams prepare for internal and external audits, reviewing project records against agreed checklists.
• Identify missing, inconsistent or expired records and track actions to closure through an audit-readiness tracker.
• Compile audit evidence packs, recording findings, owners and due dates.
• Produce user guides, FAQs and training materials for AI tools.
• Prepare and streamline business-wide reporting for all support functions, coordinating inputs and meeting tight deadlines.
• Gather, validate and analyse data from multiple sources, maintaining data models that ensure accuracy and integrity.
• Work with project teams to create Power BI dashboards and reports as required.
Requirements
Qualification
• Degree in data science, computer science, engineering, business management, digital technology
Skills
• Strong organisational skills.
• Attention to detail.
• Clear written and verbal communication.
• Ability to work with structured and unstructured information.
• Confidence using Microsoft 365 applications.
• A methodical approach to reviewing records and following actions through to completion.
• Strong analytical skills, with good working knowledge of Excel for data analysis and reporting.
• Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver work to tight deadlines.
• Familiarity with Microsoft Copilot, AI agents, large language models or knowledge management systems.
• Python
• Understanding of data governance, document control, quality management or project assurance.
• Knowledge of SharePoint, Teams, Power Platform or similar platforms.
• Awareness of prompt engineering, classification, tagging or metadata management.
• Experience using Power BI or similar data visualisation tools, including data modelling.
(The advert splits these into Essential and Preferred columns but the scraped text does not show which is which; the later items look preferred.)
Why Pell Frischmann?
Collaborative, supportive environment; ongoing development; Disability Confident Scheme; flexible and hybrid working.
Please remove personal details such as home address and date of birth from your CV. Applicants complete a diversity monitoring form.

Reporting Analyst - £52,000-£54,000 per annum - Permanent
Sage is a global, independent academic publisher of books, journals and library resources.
About our team
The Customer Experience (CX) team uses data and insight to understand customers and improve experiences, working with Customer Service, Operations, Technology, Data & Analytics and Enablement teams.
Could you be our new Reporting Analyst? Are you:
• Experienced in building reports and dashboards using Power BI, ideally with data from CRM, customer service or other operational platforms?
• Confident using SQL and DAX to extract, transform, analyse and present data?
• Experienced in using data to solve business problems, identify trends and support evidence-based decisions?
• Skilled in working with large or multiple data sources, including validating, cleansing and maintaining data quality?
• Able to translate business requirements into practical reporting and analytical solutions?
• Someone who values accuracy, with experience producing reliable, well-documented reporting?
• A clear communicator who can make data accessible?
• Comfortable managing multiple reporting activities or projects?
Your new role
• Build and maintain reports and Power BI dashboards that give CX leaders visibility of performance and outcomes.
• Turn customer and operational data into actionable insights.
• Own the end-to-end reporting lifecycle, from sourcing and transforming data to presenting outputs.
• Improve the quality and consistency of CX data through validation, cleansing and quality checks.
• Create consistent approaches to reporting, shared definitions, metrics and KPIs.
• Partner with stakeholders to translate business questions into analytical solutions.
• Deliver reporting projects and ad-hoc analysis.
Reasonable adjustments: humanresources@sagepub.co.uk

City: London
Division: Enterprise Architecture

Your opportunity
Reporting to the Head of Business Architecture, the Associate Business Architect will support efforts to establish and maintain a consistent reference model of our business with stakeholders across the firm, so we can clearly map our operating model (business process, people/organisation, technology, data, services and governance). The role supports the Head of Business Architecture with managing data relating to the firm's business architecture framework, and the way business architecture is applied on change initiatives.

Ongoing activities might include
• Maintaining current state assessments using the business architecture framework
• Performing a supporting role in projects and other change initiatives where business architecture is part of the scope
• Developing innovative dashboards and decision support tools for senior executives and leadership teams
• Supporting key change initiatives, including merger and acquisition (M&A) integration activities
• Performing analysis to identify organisation improvements using business architecture frameworks, methodologies and techniques
• Canvassing stakeholder views from operations, sales, client account management, investments, financial crime compliance and legal
• Identifying trends and insights from data relating to the firm's business architecture
• Supporting the design of target operating models and implementation roadmaps aligned to strategy
• Identifying common cross-organisational needs and capturing synergies
• Creating and amending team artefacts: procedures, controls, reporting templates, terms of reference, toolsets, record management
• Document management: maintaining operating model documentation in architecture tools and document stores

What to expect
• Hybrid working, generous holiday, health and wellbeing benefits
• Paid volunteer time, professional development and qualification reimbursement
• Lunch allowance for the subsidised onsite canteen

Must have skills
• Some experience of documenting operating models, either in a business architecture role or as a business analyst/equivalent
• Good analytical skills and knowledge of MS Excel, Word and PowerPoint
• Understanding of how business and enterprise architecture toolsets operate
• Good communication and presentation skills
• Strong team ethic
• Problem-solving
• Wanting to stay curious, ask questions and learn new skills
• Good organisation skills: time management, estimating, planning
• Positive attitude
• Strong work ethic
• Ability to prioritise and juggle priorities

Nice to have skills
• Aligned project certification
• Experience with Microsoft Visio and/or other process capture tools
• Background in financial services (ideally asset management)

Supervisory responsibilities: No
Annual bonus: may be eligible for a discretionary bonus. All applications are subject to background checks. "Don't worry if you don't think you tick every box, we still want to hear from you!"

jd_full:
PRUDENTIAL REPORTING ANALYST
We are looking for a Prudential Reporting Analyst in Wealth Management.
About Us
Schroders is a global investment manager which provides active asset management, wealth management and investment solutions. Established in 1804, we have around 5,500 people across 36 global locations. Our HQ is in the City of London.
The team
You will join the Wealth Management Finance team. The role sits within the Prudential Reporting Team, which is responsible for delivering accurate, timely and controlled prudential regulatory reporting for Wealth Management entities, working closely with Commercial Finance, Entity Finance, Treasury, Banking, Lending, Risk, Technology and Group Finance.
What you'll do
The role provides broad exposure across prudential regulation, treasury and risk reporting. You will support the preparation and control of recurring reporting, while using technology and data to enhance, automate and improve reporting processes, supported by the wider team.
Key responsibilities
• Support recurring treasury, liquidity, interest rate risk and other prudential risk reporting and analysis.
• Perform data preparation, reconciliations, validation and investigation of movements, exceptions and data quality issues.
• Maintain effective controls, procedures, supporting evidence and audit trails across assigned reporting processes.
• Support the operation and maintenance of prudential and Asset Liability Management (ALM) reporting systems.
• Identify and implement opportunities to simplify, standardise and automate reporting processes.
• Support the preparation, review and delivery of prudential regulatory returns across Wealth Management entities.
• Support broader technology and transformation initiatives, including regulatory reporting software.
• Work collaboratively across Finance, Treasury, Risk and Technology.
The knowledge, experience and qualifications you need
• Relevant academic or professional qualification, e.g. finance, accounting, economics.
• Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to work accurately with detailed financial data.
• Ability to learn new financial and regulatory concepts quickly and apply them in practice.
• Strong Excel skills, including calculations, reconciliations and data validation.
• Ability to investigate unexpected results and identify data, process or calculation issues.
• Good organisational skills, with the ability to manage recurring deliverables against fixed deadlines.
• An interest in technology and how it can be used to improve accuracy, efficiency and control.
The knowledge, experience and qualifications that'll help
• Experience with data and automation tools such as AI, Power Query, Power BI, SQL, Python or VBA.
• Exposure to system implementation, data mapping, user acceptance testing or reporting process transformation.
We will consider flexible working arrangements for all roles.

Are you experienced in Accounts Payable or Purchase to Pay with a keen interest in process improvement and finance transformation?
W&A is partnering with a business undergoing a significant finance transformation programme to recruit an Accounts Payable Business Process Analyst on a two-year fixed-term contract.
Contract: 2-year FTC
Working Arrangement: Hybrid
The Opportunity
Working closely with the Purchase to Pay Workstream Lead, you will review, redesign and improve end-to-end P2P processes, from supplier onboarding and purchase ordering through to invoice processing, approvals and payments. You will identify inefficiencies, challenge existing ways of working and translate findings into practical improvements, and support automation, stronger process controls and standardised ways of working across Finance and Procurement.
Key Responsibilities
• Map, document and review end-to-end Purchase to Pay processes, responsibilities and controls.

• Apply LEAN or similar methodologies to identify root causes, eliminate inefficiencies and improve cycle times.

• Support the introduction of workflow tools, automation and technology-enabled improvements.
• Coordinate workstream activities, tracking actions, risks, issues and dependencies.
• Engage with stakeholders across Finance, Procurement and wider business functions.
• Support the transition of new processes into business as usual.
What You'll Bring
• Experience in Accounts Payable, Purchase to Pay, finance process analysis or business process improvement.
• A strong understanding of end-to-end P2P processes and associated financial controls.
• Practical experience applying LEAN or similar continuous improvement methodologies.
• Exposure to finance transformation, process change or project delivery.
• Strong analytical, process mapping, documentation and problem-solving skills.
• A proactive and inquisitive approach.
• Strong organisational, communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint and Word.
Why Apply?
• Develop finance transformation experience within a significant change programme.
• Ownership of meaningful process improvement activity.
• Exposure to automation, technology-enabled change and end-to-end process design.
The recruiter invites applications via CV submission (a named consultant's email is given in the advert).

We are seeking an experienced Business Analyst to support a six-month Client Services reporting and data assessment.
The role will undertake a detailed current-state assessment of the Client Services reporting landscape, creating a comprehensive inventory of client reports, the individual data components contained within them, their source systems, dependencies, ownership and distribution methods.
A key objective is to move beyond a simple report inventory and establish a clear understanding of how data is consumed across reporting, where duplication or bespoke variation exists, whether authoritative "golden sources" are being used, and where improvements can be made to data governance, validation and distribution.
The Business Analyst will work cross-functionally and cross-regionally across Client Services, the International Reporting Team, technology/data teams and external data providers, and translate the assessment into practical recommendations and a sustainable reporting/data inventory.
Reporting inventory and analysis
• Create a complete inventory of Client Services reports, including standard, master and bespoke client reporting.
• Document report purpose, audience, owner, frequency, production process and method of distribution.
• Identify the data components/data fields contained within each report and map where each component is used across the reporting estate.
• Quantify data-component reuse and the degree of customisation against standard or master reports.
• Identify clusters of materially similar reports and opportunities for standardisation or consolidation.
Data lineage, ownership and governance
• Map each data component back to its originating source and identify the authoritative or golden source where one exists.
• Document movement and dependencies between source data, intermediate processes and final client reports.
• Identify the owner or accountable provider for each data component.
• Assess ownership, governance, quality controls, validation, completeness and accuracy of data components.
• Highlight gaps in ownership, governance, validation and data lineage.
Current-state process assessment
• Map existing report production and distribution processes across Client Services, the International Reporting Team and third-party providers.
• Identify manual interventions, duplicate processes, reconciliations and dependencies.
• Identify key operational risks, inefficiencies and opportunities to simplify.
Inventory and workflow solution
• Define the requirements for a sustainable inventory/workflow capability rather than a static spreadsheet.
• Structure the inventory so that reports, data components, sources, owners, controls and dependencies can be linked and analysed.
Special Factors: Hybrid working. We cannot offer sponsorship for this position.

jd_full:
Be Part of Something Growing - Join Stamp!
Stamp is a fast-growing, award-winning independent retailer offering stationery, gifting, printing and Post Office services across London and the Home Counties.
We're looking for a commercially minded Replenishment & Allocation Analyst to join our Supply Chain team.

The Role
You'll make sure our stores have the right stock, in the right quantities, at the right time, working closely with Supply Chain, Buying, our warehouse and store teams. You'll own weekly replenishment, stock allocations, transfers and seasonal sell-through, and produce the reporting and analysis that supports trading and planning decisions.

What You'll Be Doing
• Managing weekly store replenishment
• Planning and managing seasonal allocations, stock transfers and store openings
• Monitoring stock availability, sales and seasonal sell-through, and taking action
• Working with suppliers and our central warehouse to keep stock flowing
• Producing weekly trading reports and supporting monthly supply chain planning
• Maintaining accurate stock data, reporting and processes
• Building strong working relationships with stores, warehouse and wider teams

What We're Looking For
• 1-3 years' experience in retail allocation, replenishment or stock control
• Advanced Excel skills; Power Query experience would be a big advantage
• Strong numerical skills and excellent attention to detail
• A proactive approach and confidence to take ownership
• Commercial awareness of how stock impacts sales and profitability
• Great organisational and communication skills
• Ability to manage priorities and work at pace
• A positive, can-do attitude and appetite to learn
Experience with seasonal retail, Inventory Planner or Lightspeed would be an advantage.

Pay: £30,000 per year
Benefits: employee discount, health & wellbeing programme, referral programme, work from home

Application questions
• Do you have the right to work in the UK for at least the next 24 months?
• Do you have 1-3 years' experience in retail allocation, replenishment or stock control?

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Stoke Newington

• Strong understanding of programme governance, reporting and quality assurance.
• Experience coordinating executive reporting and governance board packs.
• Experience maintaining risk and action registers.
• Knowledge of contractual change control processes and change monitoring.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management, including clients and external partners.
• Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
• Experience with Jira and Confluence.
• Proactive approach to problem-solving and process improvement.
Desirable:

Business Analyst - Newcastle
Business Architecture Senior Analyst | Early Career | Full time | Job No. R00327900 | Newcastle
Please Note: Any offer of employment is subject to satisfactory BPSS and SC security clearance which requires 5 years continuous UK address history (typically including no periods of 30 consecutive days or more spent outside of the UK) at the point of application. This relates to a specific client requirement.
Hybrid Working: This role will require you to work from our Newcastle, Cobalt Business Park office 3 days per week.
Our Advanced Technology Centre delivers large-scale solutions for UK public and private sector organisations.
As a team
We are looking for technically orientated Business Analysts to join our Business Analysis community in Newcastle, acting as a bridge between business stakeholders and technical teams, turning business needs into well-defined requirements and designs.
As a Business Analyst, you will:
• Support discovery: define problems, explore solution options, assess feasibility, risks and dependencies.
• Apply business analysis tools and techniques to assess processes and define fit-for-purpose solutions.
• Support functional and non-functional requirements identification, elicitation and validation.
• Produce functional designs, process flows, sequence diagrams, business rules and backlog items.
• Analyse business and operational data to support insights and validate assumptions.
• Contribute to business impact assessments.
• Support business readiness, operational readiness and transition planning.
• Contribute to communications and training materials.
• Collaborate with product, UX/UI, developers, testers, DevOps and live services across the SDLC.
• Participate in Agile ceremonies and backlog refinement.
• Identify and escalate risks, dependencies and constraints.
• Develop a working understanding of APIs, databases and system integration.
• Operate in a customer-facing role with appropriate supervision.
• Advocate and contribute to AI-enabled solutions and use AI to improve delivery efficiency.
Qualification
• Strong foundational business analysis skills: requirements elicitation, analysis, documentation, validation and management.
• Translate business problems into clear, structured, actionable requirements.
• Produce user stories, functional and non-functional requirements, process flows, business rules and data requirements.
• Working knowledge of UML, BPMN, process modelling and impact assessment.
• Analyse business and operational data to validate requirements and highlight risks or data quality issues.
• Engage a wide range of business and technical stakeholders.
• Exposure to business impact assessments across people, process, data and technology.
• Experience using GenAI tools to accelerate requirements analysis, documentation and test case generation.
Set Yourself Apart
• Technology-enabled or digital delivery, ideally in complex or regulated environments (e.g. Public Sector).
• System integration concepts, APIs and data flows.
• Enterprise platforms or cloud (AWS, Azure, Salesforce).
• UX principles; Figma or Balsamiq.
• Curiosity about GenAI and how AI can transform businesses.
• Exposure to benefits realisation or transition into live service.
Apply via Accenture's Workday applicant system.

This role is based in the United Kingdom and as such all normal working days must be carried out in the United Kingdom.

Join us as a Lending Business Analyst
This is a key role in the team responsible for launching a new Lending product for the first time within NatWest Boxed.

You will be:
• Defining and tracking product requirements: work closely with the Product teams across the lending domain to identify, analyse, and manage detailed product requirements, ensuring alignment with business and regulatory needs.
• Lead discovery and story creation: support and lead detailed discovery sessions with the lending team, taking ownership of crafting user stories and requirements that drive the development and build of the Lending solution.

• Develop a working knowledge of NatWest Boxed and Group policies.
• Lead the technical and operational discovery for integrating Point of Sale (POS) and embedded retail finance solutions into our lending ecosystem.

The skills you'll need
• Technical understanding of how APIs, integrations, and digital banking infrastructure work. Direct experience integrating POS and embedded retail platforms is highly desirable.
• An ability to work with Product Owners to define and refine product requirements and break down high-level needs into detailed user stories and acceptance criteria.
• Strong writing skills to create clear, structured, and comprehensive requirements documents, user stories, and process flows, ensuring these requirements are testable.
• Stakeholder and communication skills with previous experience working closely with cross-functional teams (Product, Engineering, Commercial, Credit, Risk, Compliance, Legal etc.).
• A proactive approach with great attention to detail.
• Proven experience working effectively within an Agile framework/methodology.

Additionally it will be very beneficial to have:
• Deep expertise in Point of Sale (POS) retail finance products and Embedded Finance providers.
• Relevant experience in SaaS, Embedded Finance, Banking-as-a-Service.
• Familiarity with CONC, CCA (Consumer Credit Act), FCA regulations and financial compliance.

Benefits: 10% pension funding, up to 10% benefit funding, 30 days annual leave. Bishopsgate hub, London.
Base pay range: £43k - £75k/yr (Glassdoor Est.).

jd_full:
Data Analyst | 12 Month Fixed Term Contract - Howdens Joinery - Normanton

We're looking for a Data Analyst to join our Customer Service & Planning team on a 12-month fixed term contract. This is an exciting opportunity to transform operational and customer data into meaningful insight that improves service delivery, customer experience and business performance.

Reporting to the Head of Customer Services & Planning, you'll work closely with teams across the business and senior stakeholders to provide trusted reporting, performance analysis and actionable recommendations that drive continuous improvement.

Location: Normanton, West Yorkshire
Contract Type: 12 Month Fixed Term Contract (Maternity Cover)
Hiring Manager: Head of Customer Services and Planning

What will I be doing?
• Develop and maintain dashboards, reports and KPIs that provide visibility of operational, service and customer performance.
• Analyse customer and operational data to identify trends, issues and opportunities for improvement.
• Translate complex data into clear insights and recommendations for stakeholders.
• Combine, cleanse and validate data from multiple sources to ensure reporting accuracy.
• Identify data quality issues and support improvements at source.
• Automate reporting and data preparation processes to improve efficiency.
• Produce regular and ad-hoc performance reporting for leadership teams.
• Support forecasting, resource planning and workload management through trend analysis.
• Partner with operational teams to investigate root causes and measure improvement initiatives.
• Maintain governance and documentation relating to data sources and reporting processes.

What are we looking for?
• Relevant analytical experience or a Level 4+ qualification in Data Analysis, Business Analysis, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Computing or a related field.
• Strong analytical skills, with experience interpreting operational or customer data and turning insights into practical recommendations.
• Advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups and data validation.
• Experience using Power Query, Power BI and SAP to analyse, validate and report on operational and customer data.
• Experience developing KPIs, validating data and producing accurate management reporting.
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex data to non-technical stakeholders and influence decisions through insight.
• Organised, proactive and results-focused, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver continuous improvement.

What can we offer you
• Competitive Salary
• Pension Plan with a maximum company contribution of 12%
• 25 days holiday + bank holidays with an opportunity to purchase additional days
• Staff discount
• Ongoing support and development
• Free lunch at our on-site canteen
• Free on-site parking
• Friendly and supportive environment offering exceptional reward and recognition

How to apply
If you're ready to lead impactful projects and drive meaningful change, we encourage you to apply today. If you need us to make any adjustments to our recruitment process, please email the Howdens recruitment team with the job title and location.

About Howdens
Howdens Joinery is a highly successful FTSE 100 business, with more than 900 depots nationwide and more than 11,000 staff. There is a strong entrepreneurial ethos and the opportunity to develop within a fast-paced and commercial environment.

Please note that candidates applying for this role must have a valid right to work in the UK, we do not offer sponsorship of employment for any depot positions at this time. We appreciate your understanding.

Pay (Glassdoor estimate, not employer provided): £30k - £33k/yr

We're looking for a Smart Metering Asset Analyst to join our Smart Metering Programme team on a 12-month fixed-term contract, supporting the quality, governance and effective use of data across the programme and Affinity Water.
As part of our Smart Metering Programme, you'll play an important role in ensuring the information behind our smart meter installations is accurate, complete and reliable. Working closely with colleagues across the business and our delivery partners, you'll help maintain high standards of data quality, support programme reporting and provide confidence in the information used for operational decision-making, performance monitoring and regulatory audits.
This is a varied role combining data analysis, reporting and programme coordination. You'll bring together information from systems such as Qlik Sense, GIS, Maximo and Hi-Affinity to produce meaningful insights, identify and resolve data issues, support installation planning and assist with the management of delivery partner task orders.
We're looking for someone with strong, advanced Excel skills who enjoys getting into the detail of data, spotting problems, producing meaningful reports and seeing things through to resolution.

Main responsibilities
• Maintain and check smart meter installation data across programme and corporate systems, ensuring information is accurate, complete and ready for reporting and audit.
• Bring together data from systems such as Qlik Sense, GIS, Maximo and Hi-Affinity to produce reports and updates on installation activity and programme performance.
• Identify and investigate missing, inconsistent or incorrect information, working with internal teams and delivery partners to resolve issues.
• Support the Delivery Lead with planning installation activity across delivery partner areas.
• Assist with the creation and management of delivery partner task orders, ensuring scope, deliverables and timescales are clearly documented.
• Support task order close-out by gathering documentation, checking completed work and following up on any outstanding actions.
• Help maintain data policies, procedures and guidance to support regulatory and contractual requirements.
• Work collaboratively with Smart Metering colleagues, IT, commercial teams and delivery partners to understand data requirements.
• Identify opportunities to improve data processes, reporting tools and ways of working across the programme.

Key requirements - Experience and knowledge
• Experience working with data, records or reporting within an administrative, operational or programme environment.
• Advanced Excel skills, with experience using formulas, pivot tables, lookups, filters and data validation.
• Experience checking information for accuracy and completeness, identifying discrepancies and following these through to resolution.
• Experience using Qlik Sense, GIS, Maximo, Hi-Affinity or similar business systems would be desirable.
• Experience working in an Agile delivery environment would be desirable.

Skills and competencies
• Ability to analyse data from multiple sources, identify trends, gaps or inconsistencies and explain findings clearly.
• Confident producing clear and accurate reports that support decision-making.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing requests and meet reporting deadlines.
• Good communication and relationship-building skills.

Benefits
• Salary range £33,400 - £41,000 dependant on skills and experience
• Annual bonus scheme, 23-27 days annual leave, double match pension (capped at 12%), learning and development, family and wellbeing benefits.

WE ARE LANDSEC
We identify and shape places that create opportunity, enhance quality of life, and bring joy to the people connected to them. Our £10 billion portfolio is built around premium workplaces, the country's pre-eminent retail platform, and a residential pipeline.

LOCATION
The Insight Analyst role will be based at Landsec's head office in 80 Victoria Street, London SW1E 5JL with 4 days in the office.

THE ROLE
• Support the Insight Director with deep understanding of Landsec's workplace customers, using qualitative and quantitative data sources. Highlight office tenant (customer) trends and insights, using simple storytelling and narrative to communicate findings to the wider Landsec Workplace business, senior decision makers and external partners.
• Generate actionable insight to inform marketing, leasing, asset management, operational and investment decisions.
• Communicate these insights succinctly and effectively to Landsec stakeholders and external partners.
Support the Insight Director on key projects including the customer satisfaction survey programme, customer interviews and focus groups, future trends and impact on Workplace, centralising customer datapoints, developing customer strategies, innovating data capture and reporting using all available tools (including AI).

PRINCIPLE ACCOUNTABILITIES
Data analysis
• Use both qualitative and quantitative research methods to generate actionable insight with a key focus on qualitative datasets and research.
• Work with the Insight Director to bring together various data points to develop a single customer view.
• Demonstrate interest and understanding of property and workplace sector. Monitor market trends and send a regular update to the workplace team.
Translating research into actionable insight
• Build relationships with asset management, leasing, investment, MYO and marketing teams in London and Manchester.
• Synthesise a variety of data points and information sources into digestible, actionable insights.
• Communicate insights through written reports, contributions to presentation decks and leading presentations.
• Tailor messaging for different teams and varying levels of seniority.

ESSENTIAL CRITERIA
• Analytical expertise - experience working with both qualitative and quantitative data sets, including survey data and focus group outputs.
• Effective storytelling - translate complex data points into simple narratives and recommendations.
• Data visualisation - proficient in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
• Enthusiastic about AI - ambitious with its use to improve processes and drive data sharing.
• Survey writing expertise - ability to construct consumer survey questionnaires.
• Collaborative skills.
• Methodical with attention to detail under time constraint.
• Energised by using customer insights to solve commercial challenges.

Benefits
• Performance based annual bonus, 25 days leave rising to 27, pension up to 10.5%, private medical insurance, share plans, volunteering days.

About Us
We are a leading plumbers' merchant supplying trade and retail customers with quality plumbing, heating, and bathroom products. With a growing branch network presence, focused on providing excellent service while using data to make smarter decisions.

Company Description
At Intuitive, we are united behind our mission: we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. As a pioneer and market leader in robotic-assisted surgery (da Vinci), for more than 25 years we have worked with hospitals and care teams around the world.

Job Description
Position Objective and Summary
The Business Analyst is responsible for providing best in class analytical support to the regional leadership team of UK and Ireland. This individual works closely with our local commercial leadership team analysing complex business problems and providing strategic, data-driven guidance to decision makers.

This individual drives initiatives in support of the execution of the sales and financial strategy across the UK and Ireland region and provides data-driven recommendations to support internal strategic planning, commercial strategy, territory design, quota allocation and more.

This is a highly analytical role involving the manipulation of large data sets, a keen understanding of sales concepts, financial planning frameworks and the ability to communicate and develop meaningful work relationships with multiple executive business partners.

Roles and Responsibilities
• Develop and maintain strong business partnerships with the regional leadership team.
• Analyse complex business problems using data from internal and external sources to provide commercial insights to executive leadership.
• Identify and interpret trends and patterns in procedure, revenue and sales datasets to locate opportunities for accelerating da Vinci adoption.
• Provide analytical support to teams supporting the commercial organisation.
• Manage the goal setting process for all functions under the regional leader, aligned to commercial strategy.
• Participate in territory design, quota allocation and other sales operations activities.
• Deliver weekly / monthly / quarterly reports on key business metrics to the leadership team.
• Support month end close, budget and quarterly P&L forecasting activities.

Qualifications
Required Knowledge, Skills and Experience
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Finance or related field.
• 1-3 years of Business Analytics or Financial Planning and Analysis work experience.
• Quick learner and ability to drive successful results with limited supervision.
• Demonstrated ability to work in a fast paced and complex team environment.
• Strong analytical skills with proficiency in MS Excel and experience building financial models involving complex formulas and large data sets.
• Ability to discern consistently strategic insights from data analysis.
• Ability to support and prioritise multiple projects concurrently.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English, including interacting with senior leadership.
Preferred Knowledge, Skills and Experience
• Master's degree in Business, Economics, Finance or related discipline is a plus.
• Experience within the medical / pharmaceutical environment is a plus.
• Proficiency with data visualisation tools such as Tableau; CRM such as Salesforce; planning tool such as Anaplan is a plus.

Additional Information

Business Intelligence Analyst - Barbour - South Shields

Position Overview
We have an exciting opportunity for a Business Intelligence Analyst to join our IT team here at our Head Office in South Shields. This role will be key to delivering reporting, dashboard and analytic solutions that support decision-making across the business. Working closely with stakeholders across multiple functions, the successful candidate will transform business requirements into meaningful insights, develop robust reporting solutions and help colleagues maximise the value of data.
• The role is based at our Head Office in South Shields and the expectation is 4 days in the office and 1 day of home working.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
• Design, develop and maintain BI and reporting solutions using Qlik Sense, QlikView, Power BI and SSRS.
• Gather, analyse and document business requirements and translate them into effective reporting and dashboard solutions.
• Develop and maintain data models, KPIs, measures and reporting structures to support business performance.
• Deliver dashboards and reports for assigned business areas, managing work independently and ensuring high-quality outputs.
• Investigate and resolve reporting and data issues, identifying root causes and implementing solutions.
• Support the development and maintenance of ETL and data integration processes.
• Perform data analysis and communicate findings and insights clearly to business stakeholders.
• Apply reporting standards, KPI definitions and data quality controls across solutions.
• Maintain report documentation, data definitions and reporting catalogues.
• Provide guidance, training and support to help users maximise self-service reporting capabilities.
• Support and mentor Associate BI Analysts, sharing knowledge and best practice.
• Collaborate with IT colleagues and business stakeholders to continuously improve reporting and analytics capabilities.

Skills and Experience
• Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Analytics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
• Proven experience delivering BI and reporting solutions within a commercial environment.
• Strong experience with Power BI, Qlik Sense and/or QlikView.
• Experience of SSRS reporting development.
• Knowledge of SQL and relational databases.
• Understanding of data modelling, dimensional modelling and data warehousing concepts.
• Experience working with ETL and data integration processes.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail.
• Ability to engage confidently with stakeholders at all levels and translate business needs into technical solutions.
• Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
• Experience working with ERP-based data including sales, stock and finance would be advantageous.
• Exposure to Azure Data Factory, Microsoft Fabric or Azure data services would be beneficial.
• Awareness of UK GDPR and secure data handling practices.

Benefits
• Discretionary Company bonus scheme
• Staff Discount
• Staff Shop
• Healthcare Cash Plan
• 25 days holiday as standard increasing with length of service plus bank holidays
• Access to training and development activities to support your career development
• Free onsite parking
• Subsidised canteen
• Operate hybrid and flexible working
• 4pm finish on a Friday
• Wellbeing support

Additional Information
Note: In the event that a sufficient volume of suitable applications are received, the post may close prior to the specified closing date. Please apply as soon as possible if interested.

Southampton, Store Support Office

Reporting into the Digital Insights Lead, the Digital Insights Analyst is responsible for delivering high quality analysis and insight to support Digital, Ecommerce and wider business priorities. • Interpret internal and external data sources, using tools such as SimilarWeb, to identify opportunities, risks and market developments.

Key Business Relationships

• Experience in digital and ecommerce analytics: customer behaviour, onsite journeys, trading performance and digital optimisation.

About The Role
FDM is a global business and technology consultancy seeking a PMO Analyst to work for our client within the public sector. This is initially a contract until 31 March 2027, with very good prospects to extend, and will be a remote role.

Our client is seeking an experienced PMO Analyst to support the delivery of complex digital and technology programmes. You will work closely with project and programme teams, providing effective governance, controls, reporting and coordination across delivery activity. The role would suit an established PMO professional who is comfortable taking ownership of their work and operating independently within a complex stakeholder environment. Previous government or wider public-sector experience would be advantageous but is not essential.

Responsibilities
• Maintain effective project controls, including RAID logs, actions, dependencies, milestones and delivery documentation.
• Produce clear project and programme reporting, providing stakeholders with accurate visibility of progress, risks and upcoming priorities.
• Coordinate governance activities including meetings, reporting cycles, action tracking and maintenance of key project artefacts.
• Engage with project managers, delivery teams and stakeholders to gather updates, resolve information gaps and support effective decision-making.
• Support planning and delivery throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring agreed PMO standards and governance processes are consistently followed.

About You
• Strong practical experience working within a PMO, Project Support Officer or similar project delivery role, with evidence of taking ownership rather than providing purely administrative support.
• Good experience across project governance, RAID management, reporting, planning and dependency tracking, with the ability to maintain accurate project controls.
• Confident stakeholder management and communication skills, including experience working with project managers, delivery teams and senior stakeholders.
• Working knowledge of established delivery approaches such as Agile and/or PRINCE2, with experience applying delivery methodologies in a working environment.
• Desirable: Previous experience supporting government, public-sector or complex digital and technology transformation programmes.

About Us
FDM is an award-winning global leader in tech and business talent solutions, with more than 35 years of industry experience, centres across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific, and over 2500 employees. Listed on the FTSE4Good Index and a 2026 Financial Times UK Best Employer.

Commercial Analyst - Operations & Business Intelligence - Ashley & McDonough - Merseyside

About Ashley & McDonough
Ashley & McDonough (A&M) is a fast-growing building services and compliance contractor delivering heating, electrical, fire safety, security and renewable energy services, primarily across the social housing sector. With over 200 employees and a growing portfolio of long-term contracts, we are expanding as part of Mecsia.

Role Overview
We are looking for a hands-on, commercially minded analyst to work with Finance, Operations, Administration and Procurement to improve contract profitability, supplier cost control and the efficient use of people, materials and time. This is a practical role: finding what drives performance, identifying wasted cost or effort and giving managers clear information to act on.

Company Benefits
• Life Assurance; Death in Service Insurance
• 360 Wellbeing App (24/7 GP appointments)
• Scottish Widows pension
• Fertility Treatment Support Leave; Paid Maternity and Paternity Leave
• Gym, fitness and lifestyle discounts
• Refer-a-friend and Employee Recognition schemes

Key Responsibilities
Commercial and Operational Performance
• Analyse contract profitability, margins, operational KPIs and performance against targets.
• Review engineer productivity, labour recovery, material use, job costs and contract efficiency.
• Produce clear weekly and monthly dashboards, highlighting variances, risks and required actions.
• Work with Contract Managers to challenge performance and turn findings into measurable improvements.
Operational Efficiency and Resource Utilisation
• Analyse first-time property access and administrator contact effectiveness (telephone, SMS, email); improve appointment confirmation and no-access rates.
• Monitor administrative workload and WIP clearance, including job completion, outstanding certificates, follow-on works and invoicing delays.
• Review first-time fix rates, repeat visits, engineer capability and van stock availability.
• Analyse scheduling, travel time, route efficiency and jobs per engineer per day.
• Assess how administration, engineering and technical resources are deployed; identify capacity and bottlenecks.
Financial Planning and Business Partnering
• Analyse actual performance against budgets and forecasts; explain variances.
• Support budgeting, forecasting, operational planning and contract financial reviews.
• Provide commercial insight to operational teams and senior management.
Supply Chain and Pricing
• Own and maintain merchant and supplier price files, agreed rates and contractual price changes.
• Analyse supplier invoices and material pricing against agreed terms; investigate discrepancies.
• Monitor supplier spend, purchasing patterns, stock consumption and supplier performance.
• Review supplier price changes and their effect on costs and margins.
Client Contract Price Files and Inflationary Awards
• Own and control all client contract price files, schedules of rates and pricing amendments.
• Manage the contract inflationary award process: track review dates and indices, calculate uplifts and prepare evidence.
• Coordinate submissions, approvals and implementation of awarded increases in systems, quotations and invoicing.
• Monitor the financial impact of inflation awards and resolve missed uplifts or discrepancies.
Business Intelligence and Process Improvement
• Develop Power BI dashboards and reports covering contract profitability, supplier costs, WIP, access, productivity, first-time fix and travel efficiency.
• Bring together data from operational and financial systems; use AI, analytics and automation where appropriate.
• Work with managers to prioritise opportunities, quantify savings and monitor lasting improvements.

Skills and Experience
• Experience in hands-on commercial analysis, operational performance improvement or business intelligence, ideally in a contract-led service business.
• Advanced Excel and practical Power BI or similar dashboard experience; able to interrogate operational and financial datasets.
• Strong commercial judgement across client pricing, inflation awards, supplier charges, labour, materials, productivity and contract margins.
• Confident working with and challenging operations, administration, procurement and technical managers.
• Clear communicator, proactive problem solver.
• Experience in engineering, building services, maintenance or construction would be advantageous.

Key Relationships
Finance; Contract and Operational Managers; Administration and Scheduling Teams; Technical Managers; Procurement and Supply Chain; Senior Leadership Team.

What Success Looks Like
• Accurate reporting and clear visibility of contract profitability, supplier costs and operational performance.
• Measurable improvements in first-time access, WIP clearance, first-time fix, engineer utilisation and scheduling.
• Delivered supplier savings, fewer avoidable visits and travel, improved margins.

Ashley & McDonough is an equal opportunities employer.

Pay: Up to £50,000.00 per year (employer provided)
Benefits: Company events, company pension, free on-site parking
Work Location: In person (Merseyside)

Job summary
We are looking for an aspiring analyst to undertake the Health and Care Intelligence Specialist Apprenticeship and develop specialist expertise in health and care intelligence. The apprentice will work within the Corporate Performance and Planning team to identify health and wellbeing related issues and advance public health and health inequality analysis and reporting.

Main duties
While undertaking a 36-month Health Care Intelligence Specialist Level 7 Apprenticeship, you will play a key role in the assessment of need within the Newcastle population, reviewing and generating evidence, supporting service evaluation, and promoting best practice in the collection and use of data. You will be employed as a Public Health Analyst, receiving a salary while undertaking fully funded apprenticeship training; 22 months will be an accelerated training phase including end point assessment. Work under close supervision of an experienced analyst and public health consultant. The successful candidate must be available to commence no later than 01 March 2027. Shortlisted candidates' details will be shared with the training provider, JGA. At the end of the 36 months the Trust hopes to offer a permanent position but this cannot be guaranteed.

Job responsibilities
Typically suits those with up to three years of relevant analytical experience (more experienced analysts considered). Training delivered remotely via live online seminars.
• Provide analytical support for Statutory and Mandatory reporting, commissioning and performance management frameworks.
• Support timely, validated performance information reported to the Board, commissioners and other bodies.
• Critically evaluate performance measures and advise senior managers and clinicians on improvement opportunities.
• Attend Monthly Quality and Performance Review meetings and produce a formal record.
• Develop performance reports and action plans with the Trust Information Services Team.
• Develop activity plans and performance trajectories for the annual NHSE planning submission.
• Improve data quality and data integrity; understand Information Governance.
• Analyse health and care datasets for trends, patterns and inequalities.
• Support Trust Business Planning, business cases, a database of investment proposals, and tender responses.

Apprenticeship eligibility
To be eligible for an apprenticeship you must:
• Have the right to work and remain in the UK.
• Have lived in the UK for at least 3 years.
• Must not be self-employed.
• Provide original evidence of required English and Maths qualifications.
Further information:
• You will not be considered if you have an equivalent or higher qualification in the same or a very similar subject.
• You must not be engaged in any other funded training or education programme.
• We cannot sponsor applicants during or on successful completion of the apprenticeship so please ensure you meet visa status eligibility.
• We cannot accept applications from student visa applicants.
If you are a Non-UK National applicant you must meet the eligibility criteria and fulfil the settlement requirements of the apprenticeship course funding. Your settlement status will need to be verified as eligible for funding by the apprenticeship provider for you to formally enrol on the course.

Person Specification

• Maths and English Language GCSE grade 4/C or above or Functional Skills Level 2
• Degree in a relevant subject, or equivalent experience demonstrating analytical capability
• Eligible and willing to undertake and complete the Level 7 Health and Care Intelligence Specialist apprenticeship

• Experience of using or willingness to learn Power BI, SQL and other analytical tools
• Ability to manipulate, validate and interpret datasets
Knowledge and Experience - Desirable

• NHS acute hospital experience; NHS data systems and Data Dictionary
• Business planning, business cases, forecasting and trajectories; tender responses

About the role
Join our Public Health Intelligence Team as a Performance Analyst on a 12-month fixed-term contract to provide maternity cover. This is an exciting opportunity to use data, analysis and insight to improve health outcomes and reduce inequalities across North Northamptonshire.
You will play a key role in monitoring and reporting Public Health performance, providing timely intelligence to support decision-making, service improvement and strategic planning. Working with colleagues and partners across the organisation, you will help ensure that high-quality evidence is at the heart of public health service delivery.

What will you be doing?
• Leading the analysis and reporting of Public Health key performance indicators (KPIs).
• Producing dashboards, reports and intelligence products that support key Public Health services and inform decision-making.
• Supporting the completion and submission of statutory returns and national datasets, including NHS Health Checks and NHS Health Visitor returns.
• Analysing complex data to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement.
• Delivering analytical projects and deep-dive investigations to support service planning and evaluation.
• Working closely with stakeholders to understand information needs and provide expert advice and insight.
• Promoting high standards of data quality, performance management and continuous improvement.

About you
You are an enthusiastic and analytical professional who enjoys turning data into meaningful insights that drive action. You have experience working with complex datasets and can present information clearly to a range of audiences, including senior leaders.
You will have strong analytical and communication skills, be comfortable managing competing priorities, and be able to build productive relationships with colleagues and partners. Experience in performance, business intelligence, public health intelligence or management information is essential, along with excellent Microsoft Office skills and a commitment to evidence-based decision-making.
Experience of performance reporting, statutory returns, Local Government data, or data/intelligence tools such as Power BI, RStudio or SQL would be advantageous.

• a competitive salary
• a pension scheme with a significant employer contribution, life cover and ill-health protection
• opportunities to develop your skills, knowledge and potential in a large unitary council
• generous leave entitlement (28 days, rising to 33 days) and bank holidays, plus the option to buy up to an extra 10 days
• hybrid and flexible working arrangements, where practicable for service needs

Data Analyst (Complaints) - London Borough of Islington - Islington

About The Role
Do you enjoy turning data into useful insights? Can you spot patterns, explain what they mean and use evidence to help improve services?

We're looking for a confident and curious Complaints Analyst to join us on a 12-month fixed-term contract. You'll help us understand what complaints and members' enquiries are telling us and use that insight to support better services and experiences for Islington residents.

You'll work with data from across the service, bringing information together and looking beyond the numbers to understand trends, themes and areas for improvement.

As part of the role, you'll:
• collect, organise and analyse complaints and members' enquiries data
• identify trends, patterns and emerging issues
• turn complex information into clear and meaningful insights
• produce high-quality analysis, reports and presentations for different audiences
• make practical, evidence-based recommendations to support service improvement
• work with colleagues across different disciplines to understand their needs and provide useful analysis
• help strengthen how we use data and intelligence to understand and improve our services.

You'll be comfortable working with numerical information and have experience of managing and analysing data. Just as importantly, you'll be able to explain your findings clearly. Good analysis is not only about producing numbers; it's about helping people understand what those numbers mean and what they can do differently as a result.

You'll be joining a multidisciplinary team. You'll need good attention to detail, but you'll also be able to step back and see the bigger picture.

Your experience could come from complaints, performance, insight, research, data analysis or another environment where you've used evidence to understand issues and recommend improvements. What matters is your ability to work confidently with data and turn your findings into information that others can use.

For further information or an informal conversation about the role, contact the named hiring contact in the advert.

Note to Recruitment Agencies: we are managing the recruitment process internally.

Our offer to you
• Up to 31 days leave per year, increasing to 36 days after five years of local government service

About Allica Bank
Allica is the UK's fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.
Role Description
As a member of Allica's Operational Excellence and Procedures team, you'll help Operations make better decisions and deliver better outcomes through data. You'll turn operational information into clear insight that helps teams understand performance, answer business questions and identify where to improve. You'll also help good improvement ideas become well evidenced opportunities for change, giving Product teams the information they need to assess and prioritise them.
You'll make a lasting difference by building trusted reporting and helping colleagues become more confident and self-sufficient with data. This role would suit a business analyst or junior project manager who enjoys connecting business needs with data and technology, and thrives in a fast-moving environment.
Principal Accountabilities
• Build and develop reports in Looker that give Operations reliable, relevant insight not just access to pre-built dashboards.
• Investigate operational questions, uncover trends and explain what the data means, so teams can make informed decisions and take action.
• Work with colleagues to understand business needs and translate them into clear reporting, business and technical requirements.
• Manage the assessment process for BAU operational excellence ideas, helping quantify their potential value and impact.
• Share clear, consistent assessments with Product teams to support informed prioritisation.
• Help Operations colleagues interpret data, build their data literacy and answer more questions independently.
• Identify opportunities to improve reporting, processes and the way operational information is used.
• Stay focused and deliver useful outcomes as priorities shift and the business changes.
Personal Attributes & Experience
• Highly data literate, with the curiosity to explore the detail, challenge assumptions and find meaningful answers in data.
• Experienced in building reports with Looker.
• A clear communicator who can make data understandable and useful for a range of audiences.
• Able to gather requirements and bridge the needs of business stakeholders and technical teams.
• A practical problem solver who can structure ambiguous questions and turn findings into recommendations.
• Self-motivated and organised, with the judgement to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, changing environment.
• Collaborative and keen to help others become more confident and self-sufficient with data.
• Banking operations experience is a bonus.
• Experience as a business analyst, junior project manager or in a similar role connecting business requirements with technical delivery would be valuable.

Flexible working

Operations Analyst - dusk - Doncaster

An exciting opportunity has arisen to join our team as Operations Analyst working in Doncaster as part of our Operations Team.

Salary: Competitive salary + excellent benefits package (Glassdoor shows £33k/yr, employer provided)

You'll use data, reporting and insight to monitor performance, identify trends and highlight opportunities to improve productivity, accuracy and efficiency. Working closely with the Warehouse Management team and wider Supply Chain function, you'll turn data into practical recommendations that can make a real difference on the warehouse floor.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working with data but also wants to be close to the operation, understand how things work and play an active role in improving them.

Role Responsibilities
• Analyse warehouse performance data to identify trends, inefficiencies and opportunities for improvement.
• Monitor key operational KPIs including productivity, accuracy, order volumes, pick rates, stock movements and delivery performance.
• Produce and maintain regular reports and dashboards, providing clear insight into warehouse performance.
• Work closely with Warehouse Management and operational teams to understand performance issues and identify practical solutions.
• Analyse labour, workflow and resource requirements to help ensure the warehouse is operating efficiently.
• Identify opportunities to improve warehouse processes, reduce costs and increase productivity.
• Support the implementation of new processes, systems and operational initiatives within the warehouse.
• Monitor stock movement and warehouse activity, highlighting any discrepancies, trends or potential risks.
• Track operational performance against agreed targets and provide regular updates to relevant stakeholders.
• Assist with forecasting workload and capacity requirements, particularly during peak trading periods.
• Support continuous improvement projects, measuring the impact of changes and reporting on results.
• Ensure warehouse data is accurate, up to date and consistently recorded across relevant systems.
• Identify opportunities to automate or improve reporting processes to make information more accessible and efficient.
• Support in formatting findings and recommendations so they can be presented to Warehouse and Senior Management teams.
• Support ad-hoc analysis and reporting as required to help inform operational and commercial decisions.

About You
• Experience in an analytical, operational or warehouse-focused role.
• Strong analytical skills and confidence working with large volumes of data.
• Excellent Excel skills and the ability to manipulate and interpret data effectively.
• Experience creating reports.
• A strong eye for detail and a methodical approach to problem solving.

Position: Product Analyst
Location: Sutton Coldfield, Birmingham - from next year Aston, Birmingham (Hybrid flexible working, 3 days office)
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

Help us make better decisions for the customers we serve.
Every funeral plan we offer represents a promise to a customer and their family. It's our responsibility to make sure that promise continues to be met. That means understanding how our products perform, identifying where things can be improved, and ensuring we're always delivering fair outcomes.

As our Product Analyst, you'll be the person turning information into insight, spotting trends, asking the right questions and helping us understand what's really happening across our products and customer journeys. Whether it's improving customer experience, supporting regulatory requirements or making sure our products continue to offer fair value, your work will help shape the decisions we make every day.

What your days will look like
• Monitor how our funeral plan products are performing and identify trends, risks and opportunities.
• Analyse customer outcomes to help ensure we're delivering fair value and meeting regulatory expectations.
• Produce reports and dashboards that help stakeholders understand what's happening and where action is needed.
• Investigate complaints, customer feedback and operational performance to identify root causes and recommend improvements.
• Support product governance activities, including product reviews and ongoing monitoring.
• Work with colleagues across Product, Operations, Compliance, Risk and Technology to improve products and customer experiences.
• Track actions and recommendations to make sure improvements are delivered.
• Support internal audits, regulatory requests and governance forums with accurate information and analysis.
• Help us make evidence-based decisions that benefit both our customers and our business.

What you'll bring
You're naturally curious and enjoy getting to the bottom of a problem. You like working with data and finding patterns, and you can explain your findings clearly to people who may not be data experts. You'll be organised, analytical and comfortable managing multiple priorities.

You'll also have:
• Experience analysing data, trends or business performance.
• Strong problem-solving and root cause analysis skills.
• Excellent attention to detail.
• Confidence using Microsoft Excel and other reporting tools.
• The ability to communicate insights clearly to a range of stakeholders.
• A proactive approach and a genuine desire to improve outcomes.

Experience within Financial Services, Insurance or another regulated environment would be helpful, but it's not essential. If you've worked in a role involving analysis, reporting, governance or continuous improvement, we'd love to hear from you.

Life Services Group brings together funeral services, crematoria and cemeteries, legal services, direct cremation and wills, including Dignity Funeral Directors, CMG, Simplicity Cremations, Dignity Legal Services and Farewill.

Job description
Terms & Conditions: 37 Hours, Permanent
Department: Digital & IT

Help us solve problems that matter
Are you curious, analytical and someone who enjoys getting underneath a problem to understand what is really going on?
We are looking for an experienced Business Analyst to join our Digital & IT team and help us design better, more efficient and sustainable ways of delivering services.
This isn't just about documenting processes or gathering requirements. We want someone who can ask the right questions, challenge assumptions and use evidence to help us understand what problem we are trying to solve and what will deliver the greatest value.
You'll work alongside project managers, fellow business analysts, data analysts, service designers and technical specialists, supporting a varied portfolio of technology, service improvement and organisational change. The role spans the full project lifecycle, including scoping, stakeholder analysis, business cases, requirements, process mapping, testing and service adoption.

What you'll be doing
You'll work closely with services and stakeholders to understand their needs, analyse data and evidence, map how things work today and identify opportunities to make them better.
You'll help us ensure the solutions we invest in are efficient, deliver genuine value and are sustainable over the long term, rather than simply digitising existing processes or solving today's problem in isolation.
You'll also be joining us at an interesting time for local government. With Local Government Reorganisation on the horizon, there will be opportunities to get involved in increasingly complex challenges, rethink how services and processes could work in the future and help shape solutions that are designed with tomorrow as well as today in mind.

What we're looking for
We'd love to hear from you if you have experience of:
• Business analysis across technology, business change or service improvement projects.
• Unpicking complex problems and turning them into clear, actionable requirements.
• Using research, data and evidence to challenge assumptions and inform decisions.
• Mapping, analysing and redesigning end-to-end processes.
• Developing business cases and assessing costs, benefits and options.
• Bringing stakeholders together to understand different needs and find practical solutions.
• Considering the wider impact of change, not simply implementing the immediate solution.
• Managing competing priorities and supporting multiple projects at the same time.
• Communicating complex information clearly and influencing people at different levels.
Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is naturally curious, comfortable asking why and motivated by making things work better.
A formal Business Analysis qualification or degree would be welcomed but we'll equally consider applicants who can demonstrate strong Business Analysis experience gained in the workplace.

Why join us?
You'll be joining a supportive, collaborative team where you'll have the opportunity to work on high-profile and increasingly complex challenges, influence how services are designed and delivered, and see the difference your work makes.
Whether you already work for Blackburn with Darwen Council or are considering joining us for the first time, if you enjoy solving problems, challenging how things have always been done and helping turn ideas into practical, sustainable improvement, we'd really like to hear from you.
For an informal conversation about the role before applying, the advert names a contact in the Digital & IT team (Hayley Roberts).
We encourage candidates to complete their application using their own words and experiences. While AI tools may be used for support, applications should accurately reflect your individual skills, knowledge, and suitability for the role.

Data Product Solution Analyst
Permanent - Full time
Manchester / Staines / Leeds
Salary starting from 44,900.00 depending on experience
The Data Product Solution Analyst is responsible for analysing and improving the operational processes, workflows and decision-making journeys supported by the Care Services data product portfolio.
Working in partnership with Product Managers, Technical Leads, Analysts, Developers and multidisciplinary product squads, the role helps ensure that data products address genuine operational problems and enable colleagues to make informed decisions, complete important activities and take appropriate action. The role investigates how work is performed today, identifies pain points, inefficiencies and unmet needs, and helps design improved future-state processes and data-enabled solutions.
Reporting to the Senior Product Manager, the role supports product discovery, definition, delivery and continuous improvement by translating business needs, user insight and operational complexity into clear workflows, requirements and solution concepts.
The role does not define technical architecture but works closely with Product and Technical colleagues to ensure proposed solutions are valuable, usable, operationally viable and technically feasible.
Key Responsibilities
Process Discovery and Analysis
• Investigate how operational activities, decisions and workflows are currently performed across Care Services.
• Engage colleagues and stakeholders to understand business needs, process variation, pain points, constraints and dependencies.
• Map current-state processes, user journeys, decision points, information flows and system interactions.
• Identify duplication, manual effort, process gaps, avoidable complexity and opportunities for improvement.
• Distinguish underlying operational problems from requested reports, dashboards, features or solutions.
• Use qualitative and quantitative data to establish a clear understanding of the problem, inform solution design and assess its operational impact.
Workflow and Future-state Process Design
• Design clear and practical future-state processes, workflows and decision journeys.
• Ensure proposed workflows consider roles, responsibilities, hand-offs, exceptions, controls and operational dependencies.
• Validate future-state designs with affected users and stakeholders before detailed delivery begins.

About AXA
AXA is a global leader in insurance and financial services, dedicated to helping customers protect what matters most to them. As the sixth-largest insurance company in the world, we provide a wide range of services, including health, car, home, and business insurance. We support millions of customers worldwide, helping them navigate life's uncertainties with confidence.
AXA Health supports members to put their health first, from individuals to huge corporates, with fast access to diagnosis and treatment when they need it.

Job overview
Are you passionate about shaping the future of healthcare? We're looking for a proactive individual to join our AXA Health within the Claims Analytics team. You'll play a key part in developing claims analysis that helps contain costs, spot changes in condition and utilisation, and monitor provider spend. Your insights will empower the business to make data-driven decisions to manage key risks and seize opportunities, ultimately driving better care and cost efficiency. You'll encompass Claims Cost Management across the business, supporting Care Co-ordination claims data, and analysing claims to support our ambitious Care and Claims Transformation Programme.

Key responsibilities
• Help develop tools and reports to manage and reduce claims costs and spot new opportunities across the business.
• Support the creation of claims insights and models to identify trends, risks, market spending, and differences in treatment, to guide strategic decisions.
• Provide analysis to care co-ordination teams, highlighting areas of underperformance, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
• Track the progress of initiatives in the Care and Claims Transformation Programme, flagging risks and recommending actions to achieve goals.
• Assist in designing and implementing new products, processes, and services, ensuring claims costs are controlled and health data is accurate.
• Offer expertise on claims for strategic projects, including forecasts and analysis of what drives claims spending.
• Ensure compliance with regulations by analysing data to identify issues affecting customer outcomes and managing programme risks.
• Build strong relationships with teams in Pricing, Actuarial, Finance, and Data, ensuring clear communication and effective claims oversight.

Work arrangements
At AXA we work smart, empowering our people to balance their time between home and the office. You'll work at least two days a week (40%) away from home, moving to three days a week (60%) from January 2027. Away from home means attending the office, visiting clients or attending industry events.

Your skills & experience
• Knowledge and experience of insurance claims processes and broader business operations.
• Analytical skills to identify clinical issues, spend trends, condition changes, provider behaviour, and health data developments.
• Commercial acumen with the ability to translate insights into actionable recommendations.
• Experience using SQL, PowerBI and Excel to design, develop, and implement data products, models, and analytical solutions.
• Skilled at engaging effectively at all levels, including presenting to programme committees.
• Proven relationship management and networking abilities to collaborate across teams and stakeholders.
• Ability to interpret data, generate insights, and understand their impact on business strategies and outcomes.
• Current knowledge of market developments, regulatory and compliance requirements, and the ability to operate effectively within ambiguity.
As a precondition of employment for this role, you must be eligible and authorised to work in the United Kingdom.

How to apply
To apply, click on the 'apply now' button, you'll then need to log in or create a profile to submit your CV. AXA is an Equal Opportunities Employer and offers an Accessibility Concierge for adjustments during the application or interview process.

Your benefits
• Pay & Bonus: annual pay review and performance-based bonus.
• Private Medical Cover: employer funded scheme available to all colleagues.
• Annual Leave: 25 to 28 days of holiday per year, plus bank holidays.
• Wellbeing Initiatives.
• Volunteering Leave: three paid volunteering days per year.
• Paid parental & carer's leave: 26 weeks' maternity leave, 8 weeks' co-parent leave, 5 days' carer's leave.
